summary: Continuation of the He18 extraction with explicit integral compact-open volume, finite-sum convolution and local-unit proofs; a twisted-commutator proof without stable-subgroup assumptions; the actual rational-character apartment and finite affine kernel; and compatible Lang solutions via finite inverse systems. All earlier items, routes, source findings and central-twist/rigid-presentation repairs are preserved. Actual BT/congruence producers and the HN14 transfer remain open, so the extraction stays partial.

items.name: Barycentric congruence filtration
items.statement: For the fixed alcove barycenter let I_n be the integer-depth Moy–Prasad filtration, with I_0=I in the paper's convention and positive levels compact open pro-p. The filtration is normal in I, θ-stable, descending and cofinal among identity neighborhoods; record root-depth and toral coordinates rather than an unspecified congruence subgroup. Required Ω compatibility: every chosen length-zero normalizer representative, and its θ-image, normalizes I_n; for a nonfaithful or enlarged apartment specify how the barycentric filtration is transported. Use the barycenter in the reduced apartment and the separate toral depth filtration. Central translations need not fix any point of the enlarged apartment; their filtration compatibility must be proved from the toral and root coordinates.

items.name: Finite Ω-cosets under an explicit guard
items.statement: If (1 − θ)Ω is finite — equivalently, if the fibres of Ω → Ω_θ are finite — then the elements of a θ-twisted conjugacy class of W̃ lie in finitely many W_a-cosets. The hypothesis holds for θ = id and whenever Ω is finite, and it is not implied by the finite order of θ: the image in W̃/W_a ≅ Ω of the twisted class of w′ is κ(w′) + (1 − θ)Ω, not the θ-orbit of κ(w′).

items.name: Failure of arbitrary-ring Howe finite generation
items.statement: For the datum of F5 with X = I = Z_2^×, evaluation at 1_I carries the invariant distributions supported on I onto Ann_R(t) = V, which is not a finitely generated R-module. items.name: Newton centralizer Levi
items.statement: For ν=(κ,v), let M_ν be the F-Levi subgroup centralizing v, with rational points generated by Z_G(A)(F) and root subgroups U_a(F) for roots satisfying 〈v,a〉=0. M_ν=G precisely when v is central, i.e. annihilates every relative root.

items.name: Standard parahoric pair
items.statement: A standard pair (P,τ) consists of a parahoric P containing I and τ∈Ω with τ̇θ(P)τ̇⁻¹=P. Its finite Weyl group W_P is normalized by Ad(τ)θ, not necessarily by Ad(τ) alone. Let StP be all such pairs; it may be infinite through Ω.

items.name: Finite clopen refinement of a compact support
items.statement: Let X be locally profinite and {U_a} an open cover. Every compactly supported locally constant f on X admits a finite decomposition f=Σ f_b with disjoint compact-open supports, each contained in some U_a. Any two such decompositions admit a common finite clopen refinement.

items.name: Finite affine errors separate distinct translation slopes
items.statement: Let V be a real vector space, W0 a finite linear group, and A,B finite sets of affine maps with linear parts in W0. If, for infinitely many positive integers m, there are a∈A,b∈B with t^(mλ2)=a t^(mλ1)b as affine maps, then λ2 lies in the W0-orbit of λ1. This includes central directions and does not require the affine action to be faithful.

items.name: Existing positive modular character
items.statement: For a locally compact topological group, the modular character is a multiplicative map to nonnegative reals, is strictly positive, and scales right translates of any inner-regular left Haar measure. Its convention is mu(A g^-1)/mu(A). The pinned file does not prove continuity.

items.name: Existing inner-regular Haar uniqueness
items.statement: For a locally compact topological group with its Borel measurable structure, if mu is Haar and muprime is left invariant and finite on compact sets, both inner regular, then muprime=haarScalarFactor(muprime,mu) smul mu. This is an ENNReal-valued measure theorem, not an arbitrary-ring integration construction.

items.name: Existing finite inverse-system nonemptiness
items.statement: For any directed preorder J and a functor F:J^op→Type with every F(j) finite and nonempty, F has a compatible section. No transition-surjectivity hypothesis is required.

items.name: Normalized integral compact-open volume
items.statement: Let G be Hausdorff locally profinite and P a compact open pro-p subgroup. Define a left-invariant finitely additive volume on compact open subsets with values in Z[1/p], normalized by v(P)=1. For compact open K, v(K)=[K:K∩P]/[P:K∩P]. For compact-open U express U as a finite disjoint union of left cosets xL for a common open L⊂P and sum v(L).

api.name: He18.integralVolume_normalize

api.name: He18.integralVolume_compactSubgroup
api.statement: For compact open K, v(K)=[K:K∩P]/[P:K∩P].

api.name: He18.integralVolume_leftTranslate
api.statement: For g∈G and compact open U, v(gU)=v(U).

items.name: Index refinement and uniqueness of normalized volume
items.statement: The H14 volume is well-defined and finitely additive. It is the unique left-invariant compact-open volume valued in a Z[1/p]-module after specifying v(P). Every compact open pro-p subgroup has volume a power of p, hence a unit after any Z[1/p]-algebra base change.

items.name: Unimodularity from extended Iwahori generators
items.statement: Suppose G has a compact open I, an Iwahori–Bruhat decomposition with extended Weyl group Wa⋊Omega, simple lifts n_s with n_s²∈I, and lifts of Omega normalizing I. Then G is unimodular. In particular the local reductive datum A2/A5/A7 has this property.

items.name: Normalization preserved by an Iwahori-stabilizing automorphism
items.statement: If alpha is a continuous group automorphism preserving a compact open I, the normalized rational volume is alpha-invariant. This holds even when the image of v(I) is zero in R. For a unimodular G the volume is also right-translation and inversion invariant.

items.name: Finite-sum integration with arbitrary module coefficients
items.statement: For any Z[1/p]-algebra R and R-module M with the discrete topology, define integral:C_c(G,M)→M by integral f=v_R(U) sum_(xU in supp(f)/U) f(x), where U⊂P is a common right-invariance subgroup. This is independent of representatives and U and is R-linear.

items.name: Convolution has compact support and finite levels
items.statement: For f,h∈C_c(G,R), convolution from H16 is locally constant with support contained in supp(f)supp(h). If f is left U-invariant and h is right V-invariant, then f*h has the same left U and right V invariance.

items.name: Associativity of integral convolution
items.statement: The finite-sum convolution is associative and R-bilinear on C_c(G,R). No compact-open volume other than a pro-p level is inverted.

items.name: Coefficient base change for compact test functions
items.statement: For B=Z[1/p] and any commutative B-algebra R, C_c(G,B) tensor_B R→C_c(G,R), f tensor r↦(g↦f(g)r), is an isomorphism of modules and respects convolution. No flatness of R is required.

items.name: Cofinal pro-p local units
items.statement: For a compact open pro-p U put e_U=v_R(U)^-1 1_U. Then e_U*e_U=e_U. Left-U-invariant f satisfies e_U*f=f; right-U-invariant f satisfies f*e_U=f. Every finite family of compact tests admits a common two-sided unit e_U.

items.name: Convolution twist automorphism
items.statement: For unimodular G, a measure-preserving continuous automorphism theta and a character omega:G→R× with open kernel, define tau(f)(g)=omega(theta^-1(g))^-1 f(theta^-1(g)). This is an R-linear convolution-algebra automorphism. It need not have finite order, and omega need not be theta-invariant.

api.statement: If omega is constant on compact open X, tau(1_X)=omega(X)^-1 1_(theta(X)).

api.name: He18.convolutionTwist_mul

items.name: Action relations from asymmetric local units
items.statement: Under H21, for f and x choose compact open pro-p U⊂ker(omega) with f left U-invariant and right theta(U)-invariant. Put a=delta_x*e_U and b=f*delta_(theta(x)^-1), where these denote actual translated compact functions, not Dirac test functions on a nondiscrete group. Then omega(x)(a*b-b*tau(a))=T_xf-f.

items.name: Rational-character translation lattice of the actual minimal Levi
items.statement: For Z=Z_G(A), use V=X_*(A) tensor R and the finite-index restriction X_F^*(Z)⊂X^*(A). Define v:Z(F)→V by chi(v(z))=-ord_F(chi(z)) for rational characters chi of Z. Its image Lambda is a full lattice. The quotient N(F)/Z_c, Z_c=ker(v), acts affinely on A and is an extension of W0 by Lambda; no splitting is asserted.

items.name: Finite kernel of the actual affine action
items.statement: For local F, the action Wtilde=N(F)/Z0→Aff(A) has kernel Z_c/Z0, a finite group: Richarz identifies Z_c as the unique maximal compact subgroup of Z(F), and Z0 is its open compact parahoric subgroup. The image has translation lattice Lambda and finite linear quotient W0.

items.name: Newton displacement for a possibly nonfaithful affine action
items.statement: Let phi(v)=L v+c be an affine automorphism with L of finite order d. Then phi^d is translation by lambda=sum_(i=0)^(d-1)L^i c and nu=lambda/d. This vector is independent of the annihilating power d. Affine conjugation by a map with linear part M sends nu to M nu. Finite kernels in the acting group do not affect this construction; central directions are retained.

items.name: Imported finite-field Lang surjectivity
items.statement: For a smooth connected affine algebraic group H over F_q, z↦z^-1 Frob_q(z) is surjective on H(overline(F_q)). Reuse the same generic supplier identified in PAPER-KISIN-ZHOU-25/R14; this is an additional proof source, not a second Lang owner.

items.name: Finite Lang solution torsors
items.statement: For an affine algebraic group H/F_q of finite type and a∈H(overline(F_q)), if S_a={z:z^-1F(z)=a} is nonempty then it is a left H(F_q)-torsor. In particular S_a is finite. Connectedness is needed for L19 nonemptiness, not for this fiber identity.

items.name: Compatible Lang solutions in inverse limits
items.statement: Let (H_j) be an inverse system indexed by a nonempty directed preorder of smooth connected affine groups of finite type over F_q with transition homomorphisms over F_q. For J=lim H_j(overline(F_q)), the Lang map z↦z^-1F(z) is surjective. Neither surjectivity of the transition maps on solution sets nor connected transition kernels is an additional hypothesis.

items.name: Fixed cosets from a surjective subgroup Lang map
items.statement: For a group H with automorphism sigma and sigma-stable subgroup J, if z↦z^-1sigma(z) is surjective on J, then H^sigma/J^sigma→(H/J)^sigma is bijective. Normality of J is not assumed.

items.name: Finite rational points of an affine finite-type scheme
items.statement: For an affine scheme X of finite type over F_q, X(F_q) is finite. If its coordinate algebra is generated by n elements, evaluation on those generators injects X(F_q) into F_q^n, so its cardinality is at most q^n.
